A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DISRetrieval. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–C provide readable methods, equations, algorithms, tables and figures. Renumbered and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval and QA experiments on QASPER, QuALITY and NarrativeQA, together with ablations, timing measurements and retrieved-node analyses.

after.justification: v4 reports revised English-benchmark results, Chinese QA experiments on MultiFieldQA-zh, ablations and a direct computational-efficiency comparison with RAPTOR.

M1.justification: v4 introduces language adaptation through translated Chinese RST-DT data and multilingual parser training, replacing the XLNet-base-cased backbone with gte-multilingual-base (Sections 3.1.1 and 4.1; Appendix B.2). This substantially extends parser construction. The downstream tree integration, node enhancement and evidence-selection algorithms remain.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from English training and evaluation to Chinese-augmented parser training and MultiFieldQA-zh evaluation. The added benchmark includes Chinese legal texts, government reports, encyclopedias and academic papers (Appendix B.1). The three English QA benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: The QA comparator set remains flatten-chunk, flatten-sentence, RAPTOR and Bisection, including on the added Chinese benchmark. However, v4 Table 8 adds RAPTOR as an actually measured runtime comparator; v2 Appendix C.1 reported only DISRetrieval timing measurements.

E3.justification: The reported parser configuration changes to multilingual training. Added evaluation protocols include 200 Chinese test examples with two generators and 200/300/400 context settings, plus five hardware- and model-matched runtime comparisons spanning 10K–90K words. The retained English QA splits, metrics and context budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 extends the existing scalability analysis to test preprocessing efficiency directly against RAPTOR. The hierarchy-selection, enhancement-model, parser-training-scale, Top-K and threshold ablations remain, with revised numerical evidence rather than substantially different analytical questions.

E5.justification: Both versions state that Figure 6 timing results average 10 documents per length range and report standard deviations. Neither introduces new QA seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added timing table does not establish a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 revises DISRetrieval results across the English benchmarks, enhancement-model ablation, node statistics and Figures 4, 8 and 9. For example, Table 1 QASPER F1 with UnifiedQA-3B, OpenAI embeddings and 400-word contexts changes from 41.14 to 40.74; the parser configuration also changes, limiting direct performance interpretation. New results include Chinese QA F1 of 35.25 with GPT-4.1-mini at context 400 and preprocessing times of 103.0 versus RAPTOR's 338.5 seconds at 50K words.

T1.justification: The transition-system definitions, node representations, action probabilities, training loss and tree-integration mathematics are retained. Two explicit parsing equations disappear from the main text but their relationships remain in prose and Appendix A. No substantive assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion elevate language-universal discourse parsing and cross-lingual QA to central contributions. Claims expand from improvements across three English datasets to applicability across languages, explicitly including English-to-Chinese generalization. The original discourse-guided hierarchical retrieval contribution remains.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of cross-language discourse transfer and attributes runtime advantages to fewer LLM calls and selective summarization. Its limitations explicitly restrict demonstrated language coverage to English and Chinese, discuss additional translation requirements and dataset scarcity, and acknowledge possible translation-model bias.

D1.justification: v4 adds a translation prompt, training-corpus composition and the multilingual backbone identifier. It replaces the future code/model-release promise with reported public code/dataset availability and a repository address. Documentation remains inconsistent about the translation model: Sections 3.1.1 and 4.1 name GPT-4o, whereas Appendix B.2 names GPT-4o-mini.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused discussion of earlier discourse-based QA work, including Santhosh and Ali, Xu, Nair and Du, and distinguishes evidence retrieval from prior discourse applications to answer generation. References also add Tang's hierarchical work and multilingual representations while removing Chen et al. (2024). These refine the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: Beyond the scientific additions, v4 substantially compresses and rewrites Related Work and the tree-construction exposition, revises the abstract and conclusion, and reorganizes the contribution list and experimental setup. Section 3.1.1 becomes RST Adaptation with separate granularity and language discussions, and Appendix B gains a translation subsection.

P2.justification: v4 adds Chinese QA and runtime tables, extends the dataset table, relocates existing figures, and revises captions and plot axes or labels. Table 1 now explains the Bisection control explicitly. The principal diagrams, table formats and overall two-column layout remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens applicability evidence through Chinese QA evaluation and quantifies the RAPTOR runtime comparison that v2 discussed only qualitatively. The translation prompt and reported repository access also aid reproducibility. These gains are limited by inconsistent translation-model identification and incomplete synchronization of discussion with results: Section 4.3 retains the now-incorrect claim that Llama-3.1-8B has the best 400-word recall, and Appendix C.2 still quotes v2's node statistics despite the updated table.
